subject: Record tables - looking in the wrong place

messages.author: 7ea4422e45646934
messages.subject: Record tables - looking in the wrong place
parts:
Hi all, thanks in advance for help with this question. I'm pretty new to R, so maybe this is a simple fix.

I'm trying to generate a record table from my camera trap images that are organized in a file system that is set up like this: stationID -> cameraID -> species folder -> raw images.

This is the code I am using:

LEVAS<- setwd("E:/CAMERAS/LF1")  
exiftool_dir<-"E:/CAMERAS"
exiftoolPath(exiftoolDir = exiftool_dir)
LF1<-recordTable(inDir = LEVAS,
                 IDfrom = "directory",
                 cameraID = 'directory',
                 minDeltaTime = 0,
                 camerasIndependent = TRUE,
                 stationCol = "trap")

And I get this error message: 

Warning: ArcGIS contains no images;  found 0 JPEGs
Classes : 2 images
Error in `$<-.data.frame`(`*tmp*`, "DateTimeOriginal", value = numeric(0)) : 
  replacement has 0 rows, data has 2

I don't understand why it's looking in Arc, that file system isn't even on the hard drive I am directing it to. Thoughts? Thank you!

messages.author: 7ea4422e45646934
messages.subject: Re: Record tables - looking in the wrong place
parts:
Follow up, when I check to see how many images it retrieves I get this - 

> length(list.files(LEVAS, pattern = "JPG", recursive = TRUE))
[1] 158

Which is interesting because it seems to be looking in the right place, but I have way more than 158 pictures.

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Record tables - looking in the wrong place
parts:
Hi Tara,
I'm sorry for the confusing error message. I suppose what happens is that the inDir is specified incorrectly, but I'm not sure. Is LF1 a camera trap station? If so, then inDir is specified incorrectly. inDir must point to the directory that contains all the station folders.

Here's a suggestion for how to write the code (assuming your station folders are in E:/CAMERAS


exiftool_dir<-"E:/CAMERAS"  # so exiftool.exe is in E:/CAMERAS?
exiftoolPath(exiftoolDir = exiftool_dir)  # again, only needed if exiftool.exe ist not in e.g. C:/Windows

LEVAS<- "E:/CAMERAS/LF1"   # setwd() is not needed

LF1<-recordTable(inDir = LEVAS,
                 IDfrom = "directory",
                 cameraID = 'directory',
                 minDeltaTime = 0,
                 camerasIndependent = TRUE,

stationCol = "trap")

Best regards,
Jürgen
